name: 1 Samuel

overview.author: Not stated. Jewish tradition credits Samuel for the early chapters, with Nathan and Gad completing the work (1 Chronicles 29:29). 1 and 2 Samuel were originally one book.
overview.date: The events cover about 1100–1010 BC. The book was written after Solomon’s reign and the kingdom’s division (see 27:6), perhaps around 930 BC or later.
overview.audience: Israel under the monarchy, needing to understand how God established kingship and why David’s line was chosen.
overview.setting: Israel’s hill country, including Shiloh, Ramah, Gibeah, Bethlehem, and the wilderness of Judah, with the Philistines as the main enemy.
overview.purpose: To show the transition from judges to kings, to contrast Saul (who looked like a king but disobeyed) with David (a man after God’s heart), and to reveal that God raises up and brings down according to His purposes.
overview.structure: Samuel’s life and ministry (1–7), Saul’s rise and rejection (8–15), and David’s rise while Saul declines (16–31).

items.title: David among the Philistines and Saul’s death

themes.title: God Reverses Fortunes
themes.text: “The LORD makes poor and makes rich; he brings low and he exalts” (2:7). Hannah’s song sets the tone.

themes.title: The Heart over Appearance
themes.text: “Man looks on the outward appearance, but the LORD looks on the heart” (16:7).

themes.title: God’s King
themes.text: Israel wanted a king like the nations; God provided a king after His own heart.

themes.title: Friendship and Loyalty
themes.text: Jonathan’s covenant love for David is one of Scripture’s greatest friendships.

themes.title: Waiting on God’s Timing
themes.text: David twice refuses to kill Saul, trusting God to give him the kingdom in His way.

keyVerses.quote: Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice.
For the LORD sees not as man sees: man looks on the outward appearance, but the LORD looks on the heart.
For the battle is the LORD’s.

christInBook.text: Hannah’s song ends with God exalting “the power of his anointed” (Messiah), echoed in Mary’s song (Luke 1:46–55).
David, anointed by the Spirit in Bethlehem, foreshadows Jesus, the Son of David and the Anointed One.
David defeats the giant on behalf of his people as their representative, picturing Christ’s victory over our enemy (Colossians 2:15).
Jesus cites David eating the holy bread (Mark 2:25–28).

crossReferences.note: Paul on Saul and David, “a man after my heart.”
Psalms David wrote during these events.
Samuel and David in the hall of faith.

reflection: Hannah poured out her heart to God (1:15). What do you need to pour out before Him?
Samuel learned to say, “Speak, for your servant hears.” How can you build daily listening into your life?
Saul offered partial obedience and excuses (ch. 15). Where are you tempted to do the same?
God looks at the heart (16:7). What would God see in your heart today?
What “giants” are you facing, and how does David’s confidence in God speak to you?
David refused to take what God had promised by his own hand. Where do you need to wait for God’s timing?

chapterList.title: Hannah’s Prayer
chapterList.summary: Hannah, one of Elkanah’s two wives, is barren and taunted by her rival Peninnah. At the tabernacle in Shiloh she prays in deep anguish, vowing to give a son back to the LORD. Eli the priest thinks she is drunk, then blesses her. She conceives and names her son Samuel, and after weaning him she dedicates him to the LORD.
questions: How does Hannah handle her pain and provocation?
What can we learn from her honest prayer (1:15–16)?
What did it cost Hannah to keep her vow?

chapterList.title: Hannah’s Song; Eli’s Wicked Sons
chapterList.summary: Hannah praises God who humbles the proud and exalts the lowly. Meanwhile Eli’s sons, Hophni and Phinehas, treat the LORD’s offering with contempt and sleep with women at the tabernacle. Eli rebukes them weakly. A man of God announces judgment on Eli’s house, while young Samuel grows in favor.
questions: What themes in Hannah’s song (2:1–10) appear throughout the book?
How does Samuel’s growth contrast with Eli’s sons?
What does 2:30 teach: “Those who honor me I will honor”?

chapterList.title: The LORD Calls Samuel
chapterList.summary: In a time when the word of the LORD was rare, God calls young Samuel three times. Eli realizes it is the LORD and tells Samuel to answer, “Speak, LORD, for your servant hears.” God reveals judgment on Eli’s house, and Samuel tells Eli everything. All Israel recognizes Samuel as a prophet.
questions: Why didn’t Samuel recognize God’s voice at first (3:7)?
How can we cultivate a listening posture toward God?
What courage did it take for Samuel to tell Eli the hard message?

chapterList.title: The Ark Captured
chapterList.summary: Israel loses to the Philistines and brings the ark into battle like a good-luck charm. Israel is defeated again, Hophni and Phinehas die, and the ark is captured. Eli falls and dies, and Phinehas’ wife names her son Ichabod: “The glory has departed.”
questions: What was wrong with Israel’s use of the ark?
How do we sometimes treat God as a tool rather than as Lord?
What does “Ichabod” (4:21) express?

chapterList.title: The Ark Among the Philistines
chapterList.summary: The Philistines put the ark in Dagon’s temple. The next morning Dagon has fallen face down before it, and the following day he is broken. Tumors afflict the Philistine cities, and they send the ark from city to city.
questions: What does Dagon’s fall teach about the LORD’s supremacy?
Why did God act on His own when Israel couldn’t defend the ark?
What “idols” fall before God in your life?

chapterList.title: The Ark Returned
chapterList.summary: The Philistines send the ark back on a cart pulled by two nursing cows, which go straight to Israel, confirming the LORD’s hand. At Beth-shemesh, some men look into the ark and are struck down. “Who is able to stand before the LORD, this holy God?”
questions: How do the cows’ behavior show God’s sovereignty?
Why was looking into the ark so serious?
How should God’s holiness shape our approach to Him?

chapterList.title: Samuel Judges Israel
chapterList.summary: After twenty years, Israel laments after the LORD. Samuel calls them to put away foreign gods and serve God alone. At Mizpah they fast and confess. When the Philistines attack, God thunders, and Israel wins. Samuel sets up a stone named Ebenezer: “Till now the LORD has helped us.”
questions: What steps of repentance do the people take?
What does Samuel do when the Philistines attack (7:8–9)?
What would your “Ebenezer” stone commemorate?

chapterList.title: Israel Demands a King
chapterList.summary: Samuel’s sons are corrupt, and Israel’s elders ask for a king “like all the nations.” Samuel is displeased, but God says, “They have rejected me from being king over them.” Samuel warns of what a king will take, but the people insist.
questions: What was wrong with wanting a king “like all the nations”?
Why does God say they have rejected Him, not Samuel (8:7)?
Where do you want to be like everyone else instead of trusting God?

chapterList.title: Saul Chosen
chapterList.summary: Saul, a tall and handsome Benjamite, searches for his father’s lost donkeys and comes to Samuel. God had told Samuel that this man would be the leader. Samuel honors Saul at a feast.
questions: How does God use ordinary circumstances (lost donkeys) to guide Saul?
What do you notice about Saul’s humility at this point (9:21)?
What first impressions of Saul does the text give?

chapterList.title: Saul Anointed King
chapterList.summary: Samuel anoints Saul privately and gives him signs, which all come true. God gives Saul “another heart,” and the Spirit comes upon him. At Mizpah Saul is chosen by lot, but he is found hiding among the baggage.
questions: What does God provide to equip Saul (10:6–9)?
Why might Saul have hidden among the baggage?
How does God prepare people for the tasks He gives?

chapterList.title: Saul Rescues Jabesh-gilead
chapterList.summary: The Ammonites threaten to gouge out the right eyes of the men of Jabesh-gilead. The Spirit rushes on Saul, he rallies Israel, and wins a great victory. Saul spares those who had despised him, and the kingdom is renewed at Gilgal.
questions: How does Saul’s early leadership show promise?
What does Saul’s mercy to his critics (11:13) teach?
How does Saul credit the victory?

chapterList.title: Samuel’s Farewell Speech
chapterList.summary: Samuel defends his integrity, reviews Israel’s history, and rebukes their sin in asking for a king. God sends thunder and rain at wheat harvest. Samuel encourages them: “Do not turn aside... For the LORD will not forsake his people.” He promises to pray for them.
questions: How does Samuel model integrity in leadership (12:3–5)?
What hope does 12:20–22 offer after failure?
Why does Samuel say failing to pray for them would be sin (12:23)?

chapterList.title: Saul’s Unlawful Sacrifice
chapterList.summary: Facing a huge Philistine army, Saul’s troops scatter. When Samuel is late, Saul offers the burnt offering himself. Samuel arrives and rebukes him: his kingdom will not continue, and God has sought “a man after his own heart.”
questions: What pressures led Saul to disobey?
Why was offering the sacrifice himself so serious?
How do you respond when God seems “late”?

chapterList.title: Jonathan’s Victory
chapterList.summary: Jonathan and his armor-bearer climb a cliff to attack a Philistine garrison: “Nothing can hinder the LORD from saving by many or by few.” God sends panic, and Israel routs the Philistines. Saul’s rash oath nearly gets Jonathan killed, but the people rescue him.
questions: What do you admire about Jonathan’s faith (14:6)?
How does Saul’s rash oath hurt his own army?
How can leaders’ foolish decisions burden others?

chapterList.title: Saul Rejected
chapterList.summary: God commands Saul to destroy the Amalekites completely, but Saul spares King Agag and the best livestock and sets up a monument to himself. Samuel confronts him: “To obey is better than sacrifice.” God rejects Saul as king, and Samuel grieves.
questions: How does Saul justify himself, and who does he blame?
What does 15:22–23 teach about obedience and worship?
How does Saul’s concern for his image (15:30) reveal his heart?

chapterList.title: David Anointed
chapterList.summary: God sends Samuel to Bethlehem to anoint one of Jesse’s sons. Samuel is impressed by Eliab, but God says, “The LORD looks on the heart.” The youngest, David, a shepherd, is anointed, and the Spirit rushes upon him. The Spirit leaves Saul, and David becomes Saul’s musician.
questions: What does 16:7 teach you about how God evaluates people?
Why might God choose the overlooked youngest son?
How does David’s music bring relief to Saul?

chapterList.title: David and Goliath
chapterList.summary: For forty days, the giant Goliath challenges Israel, and all are afraid. David, bringing food to his brothers, is indignant that Goliath defies “the armies of the living God.” Refusing Saul’s armor, he faces Goliath with a sling in the name of the LORD and kills him.
questions: Why was David unafraid when the whole army was terrified?
How did past experiences (lion and bear) prepare David?
What does 17:47 mean for the battles you face?

chapterList.title: Saul’s Jealousy
chapterList.summary: Jonathan loves David as his own soul and makes a covenant with him. The women sing, “Saul has struck down his thousands, and David his ten thousands,” and Saul becomes jealous. He tries to kill David, then offers his daughter Michal as a trap. The LORD is with David.
questions: What does Jonathan’s covenant (18:1–4) teach about friendship?
How does jealousy take over Saul?
How does David respond to success?

chapterList.title: Saul Tries to Kill David
chapterList.summary: Jonathan persuades Saul not to kill David, but Saul tries again with a spear. Michal helps David escape through a window. David flees to Samuel at Ramah, and when Saul pursues, the Spirit comes on him and he prophesies.
questions: How do Jonathan and Michal protect David?
How does God protect David at Ramah?
What Psalm did David write during this (see Psalm 59’s heading)?

chapterList.title: David and Jonathan
chapterList.summary: David asks Jonathan why Saul seeks his life. They make a plan with arrows to reveal Saul’s intent. Saul’s fury confirms the danger, and he even throws a spear at Jonathan. David and Jonathan part in tears, reaffirming their covenant.
questions: What did Jonathan risk for his friend?
How did Jonathan honor God’s choice of David over himself?
Who is a “Jonathan” in your life, and to whom can you be one?

chapterList.title: David at Nob and Gath
chapterList.summary: David flees to Nob, where the priest Ahimelech gives him holy bread and Goliath’s sword. Then David flees to Gath and pretends to be insane before King Achish.
questions: How does Jesus use this story in Mark 2:25–26?
What do David’s actions in Gath show about his fear?
Read Psalm 34 (written at this time). How did David process this experience?

chapterList.title: David at Adullam; the Priests Killed
chapterList.summary: David hides in the cave of Adullam, and about 400 distressed, indebted, and bitter men gather to him. Doeg the Edomite reports that Ahimelech helped David, and Saul has 85 priests of Nob massacred. Abiathar escapes to David.
questions: What kind of people gathered around David (22:2)?
How does Saul’s paranoia lead to atrocity?
How does David take responsibility (22:22)?

chapterList.title: David Saves Keilah
chapterList.summary: David asks the LORD and rescues the city of Keilah from the Philistines, but learns the people would betray him. Jonathan visits David in the wilderness and “strengthened his hand in God.” Saul nearly traps David but is called away.
questions: What do you notice about how often David inquires of the LORD here?
How did Jonathan “strengthen his hand in God” (23:16)?
How did God rescue David at the last moment?

chapterList.title: David Spares Saul in the Cave
chapterList.summary: Saul enters a cave where David is hiding. David’s men urge him to kill Saul, but David only cuts off a corner of his robe, and even that troubles his conscience. He calls out to Saul, who weeps and acknowledges David will be king.
questions: Why did David refuse to harm Saul?
Why was David’s conscience troubled over the robe?
How does David leave judgment to God (24:12, 15)?

chapterList.title: David, Nabal, and Abigail
chapterList.summary: Samuel dies. The rich fool Nabal insults David’s men, and David sets out for revenge. Nabal’s wise wife Abigail intercepts him with gifts and humble words, keeping him from bloodguilt. God strikes Nabal, and David marries Abigail.
questions: How does Abigail’s wisdom prevent disaster?
How quickly did David move toward revenge, and how did he respond to correction?
Is there someone you need to thank for stopping you from a bad decision?

chapterList.title: David Spares Saul Again
chapterList.summary: Saul again hunts David. David and Abishai slip into Saul’s camp at night, and David takes Saul’s spear and water jug but refuses to kill “the LORD’s anointed.” Saul again confesses his wrong.
questions: Why does David refuse a second opportunity?
What does David trust God to do (26:10)?
How does David’s restraint reflect faith?

chapterList.title: David Among the Philistines
chapterList.summary: In despair, David says, “I shall now perish one day by the hand of Saul,” and flees to the Philistine king Achish, who gives him Ziklag. David raids Israel’s enemies but deceives Achish into thinking he is attacking Judah.
questions: What does David’s inner speech (27:1) reveal about his faith at this moment?
How did fear lead David into compromise and deception?
When have you made decisions out of despair?

chapterList.title: Saul and the Medium at En-dor
chapterList.summary: Facing the Philistines and receiving no answer from God, Saul disguises himself and consults a medium. Samuel appears and confirms Saul’s doom: tomorrow he and his sons will die. Saul collapses in fear.
questions: Why did God not answer Saul (28:6)?
Why is consulting a medium forbidden (Deuteronomy 18:10–12)?
What does Saul’s end show about a life of disobedience?

chapterList.title: David Sent Away by the Philistines
chapterList.summary: David marches with Achish’s army against Israel, but the Philistine commanders distrust him, and Achish sends him back. God providentially keeps David from fighting his own people.
questions: How does God rescue David from an impossible situation?
What might have happened if David had fought against Israel?
Where have you seen God close a door for your good?

chapterList.title: David Strengthens Himself in the LORD
chapterList.summary: David returns to find Ziklag burned and the families captured. His men talk of stoning him. “But David strengthened himself in the LORD his God.” He inquires of God, pursues the Amalekites, recovers everything, and shares the spoil even with those who stayed behind.
questions: What does it mean to “strengthen yourself in the LORD” (30:6)?
Why did David share the spoil with those who stayed with the baggage?
How can you find strength in God when everything falls apart?

chapterList.title: The Death of Saul
chapterList.summary: The Philistines defeat Israel on Mount Gilboa. Saul’s sons, including Jonathan, are killed, and the badly wounded Saul falls on his own sword. The Philistines hang the bodies on the wall of Beth-shan, but the men of Jabesh-gilead bravely retrieve and bury them.
questions: How does Saul’s life end compared to how it began?
Why do the men of Jabesh-gilead honor Saul (see ch. 11)?
What lessons does Saul’s life teach you?

tagline: From judges to kings: Samuel, Saul, and the rise of David
readingPlan: 31 chapters: one chapter a day takes 31 days; two a day takes about 16 days. For each chapter, read it on ESV.org, then come back here for the summary, questions, and your notes.
